reviews.one_line_contribution: A reader agent given retrieved successful trajectories copies not just their procedures but the writer's exploration disposition — how long it searched and in what receptacle order — with the copy scaling with the writer pool's mean search length independently of writer identity, costing success through step-budget exhaustion, and localised entirely to the search segment so that stripping it removes the contagion while keeping most of the procedure gain.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Verified with `s2cli.py paper`: MemHarness, arXiv:2607.28272 (2026-07-30, s2+hf) — 'most existing memory-augmented agents treat retrieved experiences as static records to be replayed verbatim... frequently causing negative transfer', fixed by reconstruction. It already owns the headline that verbatim replay of retrieved trajectories harms the reader; this proposal's differentiator is only *which property* of the trajectory does the harming (the writer's search disposition) and *where* it lives (one segment), plus a dose manipulation MemHarness lacks. That is a refinement of an established claim, not a new one, which is what caps novelty at 5. Two further verified threats found by my searches and absent from the proposal's Related Work and its collision check: (a) arXiv:2607.10608 The Compliance Trap (2026-07-12, verified with `paper`, s2+hf) — a trajectory-level Enter–Propagation–Recovery framework for *how* agents consume retrieved memory, finding early adoption of retrieved content compounds forward and disproportionately harms stronger agents; this is the same 'consumption behaviour, not content' altitude as the proposal, differing in that its injected property is conflicting facts rather than wasteful search, and a reviewer will ask why the proposal's E-P-R-style measurement is new; (b) arXiv:2602.00851 Persuasion Propagation in LLM Agents (2026-02-15, found via s2+hf search, abstract summary only, NOT verified with `paper`) — reports that pre-specified beliefs injected into context produce *reduced search behaviour* relative to neutral initialisation. That is already a demonstration that a context-side manipulation moves an agent's search amount; it is belief text rather than retrieved trajectories and there is no dose ladder or segment ablation, so it does not scoop P2, but it removes the proposal's implicit premise that nobody has shown context can retune exploration. Also verified: 2604.14004 (Memory Transfer Learning — 'low-level traces often induce negative transfer due to excessive specificity', i.e. the harm-from-raw-traces finding is established, only the attribution is open), 2605.24117, 2608.11888, 2305.15717, 2411.07858. I could not verify 2605.30723, 2605.23899, 2606.19911, 2412.20193 or 2607.01225 — none are load-bearing for the novelty argument. Note that the proposal mis-describes 2605.24117: the verified record is SkillEvolBench (episodic experience → procedural skills, episode-specific drift and procedural clutter), not a finding that 'abstraction discards useful contextual cues'.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline prediction P2 fits one slope across six pools that are not the same kind of object, and the manufactured half can carry the ecological half. Three pools (W1 < W2 < W3) are naturally occurring writers with a search-length spread of maybe a few steps; three (P2/P4/P8) are the authors' own padding ladder, where the x-variable is set by construction and the extreme point is 8 inserted useless actions. A slope of beta ≥ 0.3 with a CI excluding 0 is essentially guaranteed by the padded endpoints alone, and the paper would then be titled 'You Search Like Whoever Wrote Your Memory' on the strength of a manipulation in which the authors wrote the memory themselves. The falsifying interleaving is explicit and likely: beta ≥ 0.3 significant over all six pools, but the W1/W2/W3 contrast flat within its ±0.2-step SE — at which point the ecological claim (real writers differ in disposition and the reader inherits it) is unsupported while the pre-registered gate passes. The proposal never states P2 on the ecological pools alone. Compounding this, the Gate-0 harm (P1) is confounded by tokens: padded items at fixed k=3 are longer than W1 items, and the token-matching machinery is described only for the segment split, not for the dose ladder, so a 6-point success loss at dose 8 is equally explained by context dilution or long-context degradation as by inherited search. Two of the remaining four predictions are also broken as written, as the entailment check found: P6 is arithmetically unfalsifiable (when every retrieved item in the padded-pool arm is padded, 'places padded items last' has a ceiling near 1/3, so recall ≥ 0.7 cannot occur — this violates the round's binding rule that a prediction whose falsifier no arm can produce is sent back before review), and P5's placebo is a rank-10 item that is by retrieval selection less similar to the current game than the injected rank-1..3 items, so a positive tau difference is produced by retrieval similarity plus the reader's own layout-driven order with zero copying. P4 states its retention falsifier on the W1 cells while the claim is about W3 and P8, and its 0.5-vs-0.75 band sits inside the bootstrap CI of a ±5-to-±7 numerator over a +27 denominator.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register P2 twice: a primary slope on the ecological pools W1/W2/W3 only, with a margin stated in steps that the measured pool spread can actually deliver, and the padding ladder demoted to a positive control that establishes the measurement has power. State in advance that a flat ecological slope with a steep padded slope is reported as a negative result for the paper's title claim. (2) Add the token-matched non-search padding arm described under missing_baseline so the Gate-0 harm is attributable to search content rather than length. (3) Fix P5 with an order-permuted twin of the same injected item, or with the same top-ranked item scored on episodes where it was not injected, rather than a lower-ranked placebo. (4) Rerun the read-time check (P6) on a mixed bank at a stated padding rate, or as a forced choice between the padded and unpadded version of the same trajectory with chance level named; otherwise drop P6. (5) Attach P4's retention falsifier to the W3 and P8 manipulation-only cells themselves, make the search-length clause a two-sided band around k=0 (manipulation-only items name the receptacle holding the target and can push search *below* k=0), and report the retained-gain ratio with a CI narrow enough that 0.75 and 0.5 are separable — which at ±5 net on a +27 base they currently are not. (6) Show that the foreign pools' search-length distributions actually overlap W2's before promising a disposition-matched subsample, and report the subsample's n and residual type imbalance. (7) Reconcile '400-game held-out training slice' with '674 games × 2 seeds per cell'. (8) Add 2607.10608 and 2602.00851 to Related Work and say what each leaves open.
reviews.missing_baseline: A length-matched, search-neutral padding arm: copies of the W1 pool inflated by the same token count as P2/P4/P8 but with content that carries no exploration signal — repeated or verbose reasoning text, restated task lines, or manipulation-segment filler — replayed to confirm success as the search padding is. Without it, both P1's harm and P2's slope at the padded endpoints are confounded with injected-token count, and the paper cannot distinguish 'the reader inherited a wasteful search disposition' from 'the reader got a longer, noisier context'. This is the arm a reviewer will name first, and it is cheap: the padded pools already exist and the extra cells are a small fraction of the 35. A second, near-free omission is an order-permuted version of the injected item as the placebo for P5, which is the only clean test that the reader is copying receptacle *order* rather than tracking retrieval similarity.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above the round's average — it names five queries with their class, the channel (s2+hf) for each, concrete returned IDs, and it honestly reports two queries that returned nothing rather than dressing an empty search as evidence — and I credit that. It is nonetheless incomplete in a way that matters, because two of the three papers I found sitting closest to its mechanism are absent from it. My queries, all on channel (a) the s2cli command (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace); WebSearch was unavailable in this session, so no query used channel (b). (1) 'retrieved trajectories transfer exploration behavior to reading agent search length' --recent: 2606.15367, 2604.00356 Signals, 2604.04949, 2603.24639, 2603.07853, 2601.17617, 2510.24697, 2510.11686, 2510.06534 Behavior Priming, 2506.03533 — all instil or mine exploration behaviour through SFT/RL or retrieval training; none reports in-context inheritance of a writer's search length. (2) 'in-context demonstrations cause agent to imitate demonstrator inefficiency redundant actions' (no --recent): 2608.22301, 2608.15930, 2606.15587 Perfect Demo Makes Poor Teacher, 2602.08602, 2602.03664 Mitigating Conversational Inertia (imitation bias from an agent's own context — the nearest thing in the batch, but self-context inertia, not writer-to-reader), 2406.14596 ICAL, 2205.10816 Procedure Cloning; all training-time, none measures in-context copying of demonstrator inefficiency. (3) 'agent memory replay negative transfer reconstruction MemHarness retrieved experience misalignment' --recent (closest named method): 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2607.10608 The Compliance Trap, 2605.12978 Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated, 2604.27003, 2608.12428, 2606.24595, 2606.03197, 2605.18652, 2601.11653, 2512.13564. (4) 'few-shot examples induce agent to copy demonstration length and action order behavioral style contagion' --recent: 2607.19523, 2606.19408, 2604.02330, 2602.00851 Persuasion Propagation (context intervention reduces the agent's search behaviour), 2508.01600. (5) 'reader agent inherits writer exploration disposition retrieved memory segment ablation' --recent: 2608.06811, 2607.15715, 2607.10608, 2607.08716, 2606.24775, 2606.10677, 2603.15061, 2603.04549 — nothing on disposition inheritance or segment-level attribution of harm. So the specific claim (dose-response of reader search length on writer search length, localised to the search segment) is not, as far as I can verify, already made. The weakness is not an empty search but a blind spot: the proposal's mechanism queries all use agent/memory/trajectory vocabulary and its 'home' queries all use imitation-learning and verbosity vocabulary, and neither family surfaces the papers that show a *context-side manipulation changing an agent's search amount* (2602.00851) or that already diagnose *consumption behaviour* of retrieved memory across a trajectory (2607.10608). A collision check that misses the two nearest neighbours has not fully established novelty, and I score novelty at 5 on what I verified rather than at the higher figure the proposal's 'No collision found' invites.
